goal_checks.notes: Rects leaving capture are 0-1 page-relative -- selection-to-rects.ts routes every client rect through shared/utils/geometry's normalizeRect, unit-tested including the 'measures against the text-layer container, not the browser viewport' case.

Same text and rect always give the same slug -- slug.test.ts. The order-determinism gap the plan doc left open (analyze.json NEW-1) is resolved with reading-order rank, itself unit-tested (reading-order.test.ts).
Row and outbox op land together -- insertHighlight() (task 006/007) already writes both in one Dexie transaction; this task calls it, adds no new write path.

Drawing goes through the painter only -- highlight-layer.painter.ts is the sole file constructing Konva.Rect / calling batchDraw, enforced by eslint.architecture.mjs (I17), which stayed green throughout.

Automated test at three zoom levels and after rotation -- use-highlight-layer.test.ts's dedicated g5 test, exhaustive over 3 zooms x 4 rotations, recovers the exact stored rect after a denormalize/renormalize round trip.

cross_check_against_plan.result: g1-g5 match verbatim; Blocks 012, 013, 021 -- none started, nothing here reaches into their scope.

Two layers per page followed (text layer capture only, RULE-16 respected -- no in-place geometry edit exists in this code, only insert). Slug format h-p{page:02}-{order:02}-{6} matches exactly. RULE-17: only normalized rects ever cross into insertHighlight().
bbox stored as {page, rects, color, tool}, normalized 0-1, no viewport pixels -- matches the schema note exactly; a local Bbox type + isBbox runtime guard sit at the one write/read boundary.

Followed, with one correction: the plan doc did not anticipate that the page+highlight composition crosses the document/highlight context boundary (I3). Resolved by moving composition into features/highlight and adding a renderPage injection slot to document-viewer, documented in code.json.

issues_found: No page-stage/highlighted-page Storybook/Chrome story exercising a real pdfjs+Konva render was added -- jsdom cannot run that path (same gap task 009 recorded), and the plan doc's own §5 test list does not name one for this task.

document-viewer's new renderPage slot and highlighted-page are not wired into any app route -- task 009 already left DocumentViewer itself unmounted; closing that remains open for whichever task actually ships the workspace document view.
